articles.headline: The Church, and the Moral and Social Condition of Our People
articles.author: Progress
articles.summary: It is humiliating that the greatest amount of vice and misery among our people exists in the vicinity of our churches. This is attributable to the fact, that that part of the city has stood for years in an unimproved condition. The houses, old and untenantable, have been deserted long since by respectable people, and are now rented out by rooms at an enormous rent. [Goes on to the rum shops, the landlords, tavern keepers and police officers, 'of which latter there are no less than ten in the vicinity of Sixth and Lombard streets alone', and asks each church to appoint a committee of one or two to remonstrate.]

articles.headline: Cheap Groceries
articles.summary: By reference to our advertising columns may be found the advertisement of our friend, Abraham Fields. He has opened a grocery and provision store, at 424 S. 7th St., where can be found an assortment of most articles usually found at other establishments of the kind. Mr. Fields has been long and favorably known in our midst, more especially among the subscribers to the Christian Recorder, whom he has regularly supplied for many a week.
people: grocer, 424 S. 7th St.; formerly supplied the Recorder to subscribers

articles.headline: Bishop Wayman's Appointments
articles.summary: Sunday, Oct. 8th, at Philadelphia. Morning, Bethel Church; afternoon, Union Church; at night, Wesley Church. At home, from Oct. 9th to 13th. Friday night, October 13th, at Horntown, Penna. Sunday, Oct. 15th, morning, Norristown, Pa.; afternoon, Germantown; night, Zion Mission Church, Phila. Monday night, October 16th, Lower Valley, Penna. Tuesday night, October 17th, West Chester, Penna. [Continues through Downingtown, Phoenixville, Lancaster, Marietta, Columbia and Wrightsville, Oct. 23d; a note says last week's list was incorrect.]

articles.headline: Notice (Quarterly Meeting, First Colored Wesley Church, Lombard St.)
articles.summary: The Rev. J. P. H[?]mer will hold his Quarterly Meeting at the First Colored Wesley A. M. E. [Zion?] Church, Lombard St., below 6th [?], on Sunday next, Oct. 8th. By Divine permission there will be preaching at 10 1/2 A. M. by the Rev. H. J. Rhodes, of the A. M. E. Church; at 2 1/2 P. M., by the pastor, after which the sacrament of the Lord's Supper will be administered; at 7 1/2 P. M. by the Rev. A. R. Jones, of the M. E. Church. A Camp Protracted Meeting will commence with the Quarterly Meeting, and continue several days.

articles.headline: Notice. Quarterly Meeting (Union A. M. E. Church)
articles.summary: The members and friends of Union A. M. E. Church are notified that the quarterly meeting will be held on Sunday, Oct. 15. A cordial invitation is extended to all. [Signed by the Elder; the signature is illegible in this printing.]

articles.headline: Notice (Grand presentation, Zion A. M. E. Mission Church)
articles.summary: There will be a grand presentation, on October the 15th, 1865, at Zion A. M. E. Mission Church, 7th street between Dickerson and Fo[?]ter streets, at 4 o'clock, P. M. The articles to be presented consist of a very handsome family Bible, an A. M. E. Hymn book, a picture of the reading of President Lincoln's Proclamation, an Evening Scene, and a Gold Pen. These presents will be given to the persons who shall have collected the most money for the liquidation of the debt on said church.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Richard Parker)
articles.author: Richard Parker
articles.summary: Information wanted of the whereabouts of my wife, Sophia Parker, and my two children, George Walker Parker, and Mary Fanny Parker. The boy is about fifteen years old, and the girl about nine years old. They formerly belonged to a man by the name of Thomas Keyth, who resided in Virginia, Culpeper County, four miles from the White Sulphur Springs, and who moved from there in 1860, to Winchester, Franklin County, Tennessee. I have not heard from them for three or four years. [Signed Richard Parker, 251 North 18th St., Philadelphia, Pa.; Oct 6, 1m.]
people: wife sought (formerly enslaved in Culpeper County, Va.; not a Philadelphia resident)

articles.headline: Notice (Information wanted of Matilda Waters)
articles.author: Hamilton E. Waters
articles.summary: Information wanted of Matilda Waters, who formerly belonged to a man by the name of Levin Waters, of Princess Ann, Somerset County, Md. She was married to Jeremy Horsey. She had four children when I saw her last, about 30 years ago. Also, of my brother, Simon Ceter or Simon Waters. Any information can be sent to the Book Store, No. 619 Pine Street, Philadelphia, or to Hamilton E. Waters, Erie, Pennsylvania.

articles.headline: Notice (Second Quarterly Meeting, A. M. E. Hurst St. Church)
articles.author: J. Mitchel
articles.summary: The second Quarterly Meeting of the A. M. E. Hurst St. Church will take place on Sunday, October 8th, at which time we expect to have several strange ministers to preach, the Lord willing. J. Mitchel, Pastor in charge. Sept 30, 2t.

articles.headline: Attention! Attention!! (Freedmen's Employment office)
articles.author: M. A. Williams
articles.summary: Cooks, chambermaids and waiters wanted immediately at the Freedmen's Employment office. Removed from 1115 Pine St., to 6[?]5 Jane St., 7th above Chestnut. M. A. Williams. Sept 30, 2t.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On Monday, Oct. 2d, in Philadelphia, by Rev. J. Mitchell, Mr. George King, of Lewistown, Delaware, to Miss Elizabeth Hardy, of Maryland. On September 20th, 1865, by Rev. Theodore Gould, Mr. Josiah B. Flamer to Miss Susan R. Miller, both of Burlington, N. J. On September 28th, by the Rev. G. E. Boyer, Mr. Alexander Boggs [VERIFY], of Philadelphia, to Miss A. Stokley, of Camden. On October 1st, by the same, Mr. Benjamin Posels [VERIFY] to Miss S. E. Daniels, both of Camden.

articles.headline: Bowers' Coal Depot
articles.summary: Bowers' Coal Depot. Coal!! Coal!!! Thomas J. Bowers, 634 Lombard St., has constantly on hand a full supply of the best Lehigh and Schuylkill Coal, at the lowest market price. Call and Try. Oct. 7, tf. [A new display ad dated Oct. 7; his smaller 'Coal! Coal!!' ad of April 15 (T. J. Bowers, Coal and Kindling Wood Depot, No. 634 Lombard Street) still runs on the same page.]

articles.headline: Wilson's Map-Mounting Establishment
articles.summary: Wilson's Map-Mounting Establishment, No. 31 South Sixth St., Philadelphia; I. Wilson; dated july 1, 3m. [Entered as a notice: the proprietor is not known to be Black.]

articles.headline: A Visit to Mount Holly
articles.summary: An account of a visit to Evesham and Mount Holly, N. J., on the circuit of Rev. T. Gould: at Evesham the foundation of a new meeting house, 26 by 36, is laid; at Mount Holly a good, spacious edifice, a good Sabbath school and library; they only owe about two hundred dollars, all told, and the church property is worth $2,000. [Continued at the head of page 2; the signature initials are not legible.]

articles.headline: Our Trip to and from Baltimore, Maryland. Great Odd Fellows' Celebration
articles.summary: Leaving for awhile the pleasant domestic circle of our homestead in the 'City of Brotherly Love,' on the 5th instant, we repaired to the depot of the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad, arriving there at half-past 10 o'clock, P. M. ... at half-past 11 o'clock the train started for Baltimore, having on board over two hundred colored ladies and gentlemen, in connection with over two hundred members of the Order of Odd Fellows, and arrived in that city at 5 o'clock on the following morning.
people: Grand Master, G. U. O. of O. F., of Philadelphia (printed 'James McC. Crummel')
opened the exercises (Rev.), member of the Order and Past Grand Master
marshal of the Philadelphia lodges' division

articles.headline: Absence from Home
articles.summary: The editor of this paper will be absent from home for a few weeks, and all private letters for him, should be marked 'Private,' and he will get them when he returns. Oct 14, 5t.

articles.headline: Bethel Church Appointments
articles.summary: The Bethel Church appointments for Sunday, October 15th, are as follows: At 10, A. M., Right Rev. D. A. Payne; 3 P. M., Rev. William Cooper; and at 7 P. M., Rev. James H. Muse [VERIFY].
people: preacher at Bethel (Right Rev., bishop; printed 'It. A. Payne')

articles.headline: Fall and Winter Dry Goods. Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins
articles.summary: We desire to call the attention of our readers to the advertisement of the above named lady, who is well known as one of the most enterprising and business like of our day. It is needless to mention that she has, as usual, laid in her well assorted stock for the fall and winter trade. Those of our friends who need any articles in her line of business cannot do better than to give her a call.
people: dry goods merchant, 615 Lombard St. (printed 'Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins')

articles.headline: New Fall and Winter Dry Goods (S. Shorter Hawkins)
articles.summary: New Fall and Winter Dry Goods. All the Latest Styles of Merinos, Alpacas, Poplins, Delaines, Palmettas, Casenettes, Fancy Cloths. Colored and White Flannels. ... Balmorals and Hoop-skirts. ... Gentlemen's Furnishing Goods. All selling at the Lowest Cash Prices. Call and see at the old stand, S. Shorter Hawkins, 615 Lombard Street, Philada. [New autumn wording replacing the spring and summer ad.]

articles.headline: A Mistake Corrected
articles.author: Progress
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: In the last number of the Recorder, in an article headed 'The Church and the Moral and Social Condition of our People,' you made me say that in the vicinity of Sixth and Lombard streets, there were ten police offices, which, with their officers, added to the degradation of our people. It should have read 'Policy Offices.' [Counts the rum shops: Lombard Street from 5th to 8th, 20; Sixth Street from Pine to South, 13; Seventh Street from Pine to South, 9; Pine Street from 6th to 7th, 2; total 41 (as printed; the figures sum to 44).]

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: Till-Forreson. On Oct. 5th [?], by Rev. W. Moore, Rev. A. Till, to Mrs. Margaret, widow of the late Lewis Forreson [VERIFY], and daughter of the late Charles Gardner, of Phila.
people: late father of the bride, of Philadelphia (deceased)

articles.headline: Obituary
articles.summary: Died, in this city, on Wednesday, October 4th, after a short illness, which he bore with Christian fortitude, William Moore, the son of Chas. and Emily B[?]ed, aged 18 years and 2 months. He was interred at Olive Cemetery. ... Died, on the morning of the 1st inst., of consumption, Sarah M., wife of Samuel N. Gurnlah [VERIFY], in the 19th year of her age. Died, September 22d, 1865, Julia, wife of Cornelius Thomas, aged 22 years, 7 months, and 5 days. [Her voice is missed in the choir.]

articles.headline: Notice (New York District preachers' association)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: All itinerant preachers of the New York District of the African Methodist Episcopal Church are particularly requested to meet at the Sullivan street A. M. E. Church, in New York, on Tuesday, the 17th of October, 1865, at 10 o'clock A. M., for the purpose of forming a Preachers' Association. Henry Davis, Joshua Woodlin. New York, Sept 30, 1865.

articles.headline: Tribute of Respect (Prudence Lodge, No. 11, A. Y. M.)
articles.author: Nath. L. Durham
articles.summary: At a special communication of Prudence Lodge, No. 11, A. Y. M., held at their hall, South 11th Street below Pine, on the evening of October 10th, 1865, the following preamble and resolutions were unanimously adopted. Whereas, It has pleased Almighty God, in His inscrutable wisdom to take from our midst our worthy and much beloved brother, George White, after a brief illness of twenty-four hours, therefore, be it Resolved, That we deeply mourn the loss of our esteemed and valued associate ... [Signed Nath. L. Durham, Dennis Green, Ralph G. Gilmore, Committee.]
people: deceased; member of Prudence Lodge, No. 11, A. Y. M.

articles.headline: Notice (public meeting for the National Lincoln Monument Association)
articles.author: Stephen Smith
articles.summary: A very important public meeting of the colored citizens of Philadelphia and their friends will be held at the Philadelphia Institute, Lombard street above 7th, on Monday evening, October 23d, in behalf of the National Lincoln Monument Association. Addresses will be delivered by D. J. B. Smith, the general agent of the Association, and several other distinguished gentlemen. A full attendance of the friends of progress and humanity is earnestly solicited. [Signed Stephen Smith, William Whipper, Jacob O. White (as printed).]
people: speaker, general agent of the National Lincoln Monument Association

articles.headline: Appointments (Bethel A. M. E. Church)
articles.summary: Appointment for Bethel A. M. E. Church, Sunday, Oct. 22d: Rev. H. J. Rhodes, 10 o'clock, A. M.; Rev. Wm. Moore, 3 P. M.; Rev. Daniel P. Seaton, 7 P. M.

articles.headline: A Grand Reception
articles.author: L. H. Turpin
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: On the 12th ult., the Mount Moriah Lodge, No. 35, of Pittsburgh, gave a grand reception to our Grand Worthy Senior Deacon, Aaron B. Fancett [VERIFY], Esq., of your city. The affair was rich. The old and well tried Lodge, St. Cyprian, No. 13, was also in attendance. [Supper at the dining saloon of Simpson & Billons. Signed L. H. Turpin, Western Theol. Seminary, Allegheny, Oct. 18.]

articles.headline: Notice (Bishop Wayman's appointments, Oct. 29 to Nov. 12)
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Bishop Wayman's appointments from October 29th to November 12th. Sunday morning, October 29th, dedication at Deep Cut, Camden, N. J. Sunday afternoon, Oct. 29th, Union Church, Philadelphia. Monday night, Oct. 30th, Jordantown, N. J. Tuesday night, Oct. 31st, Burlington, N. J. Wednesday night, Nov. 1st, Attleborough, Penna. Thursday night, Nov. 2d, Camden, N. J. Friday night, Nov. 3d, Bridgeton, N. J. Sunday morning, Nov. 5th, Frogtown, N. J. Sunday night, Nov. 5th, Salem, N. J. [Then Union Bethel, Washington, Richmond, and a dedication at Charleston, Nov. 12. Balt. Oct. 18th, 1865.]

articles.headline: Wanted (house-work, 2216 Green street)
articles.summary: A colored girl for general house-work. Also a good cook and waitress. To such good wages will be given. Must come well recommended. No. 2216 Green street.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: Chambers-Potts. On Saturday, Oct. 7th, by Rev. Peter Boo [?], of the Union Church, Mr. Robert Chambers to Miss Susan Jane Potts, all of Pottsville [?], Del. articles.headline: Dr. David Rosell, 907 Lombard Street
articles.summary: Dr. David Rosell. 907 Lombard Street. Office Hours, Sprech-Stunden, 7 to 8 A. M., 3 to 5 P. M., 7 to 8 P. M. Oct 21, 6mo. Philadelphia. [Entered as a notice: the advertiser is not known to be Black; the German 'Sprech-Stunden' suggests a German physician.]

articles.headline: Special Notice (Union A. M. E. Church, Coates St., all-day services)
articles.author: Richard P. G[?]
articles.summary: To all friends of religious progress a general invitation is extended to attend the Union A. M. E. Church, Coates St., on Sabbath, 29th inst. Special sermons will be preached throughout the day. Bishop Weymen [Wayman], Revs. W. Moore, W. D. W. Schureman, N. H. Turpin, D. P. Seaton, J. Hamilton, and others, are among the speakers engaged. It is hoped that a large collection will be taken up throughout the day, and the friends are asked to contribute liberally. [Signed Richard P. G[?], Elder.]

articles.headline: Notice (John Wesley M. E. Church, Shippen St.)
articles.summary: The Rev. John G. Mc[?]nff [?], presiding Elder, will preach in the John Wesley M. E. Church, Shippen St., above Seventh, on Sunday, November 5th, at 3 o'clock P. M.

articles.headline: Ordination (Pearl Street Baptist Church)
articles.summary: An ordination of deacons will take place at the Pearl Street Baptist church, (Rev. T. Doughty Miller, pastor,) on Sunday afternoon next, Oct. 29th, 1865. Sermon by Rev. James B. Simmons of the 5th Baptist church. The public generally are invited to be present. [Pearl Street Baptist is in New York; text only.]

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Joseph Green Douglass)
articles.author: Sarah M. Douglass
articles.summary: Left the Emlin Institute at Lambertsville [Lumberville], Bucks County, on the 20th of July, Joseph Green Douglass, a colored lad, aged 13 years. When he left he had on his working clothes, and was without hat or shoes. Any information concerning him will be gratefully received by his distressed relatives Sarah M. Douglass, No. 661 N. 13th street, or Elizabeth Douglass, No. 1616 Helmuth St., Philadelphia.
people: missing boy, aged 13, left the Emlin Institute, Bucks County

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: [The first three entries, by Rev. R. P. G[?], are illegible on this microfilm, one of them naming a Harris of Philadelphia and one a Malone [?] of Norristown, Pa.] On Oct. 1[?], by the same, ... of North Carolina, to Miss M... of Delaware. articles.headline: Colored Soldiers! Welcome! Welcome!! (Harrisburg reception, Nov. 14)
articles.summary: 'He who defends freedom, is worthy of all its franchises.' The Capital of the old Keystone, greets you. Under the auspices of the 'Garnet League,' of Harrisburg, many of the friends of Pennsylvania, desiring to express some recognition of the services of our brave colored soldiers, have contributed liberally to give you a Complimentary Reception, a Free Dinner, and an Oration Welcome, in the city of Harrisburg, on Tuesday, November 14th, 1865. [Prof. William Howard Day to deliver the oration; Rev. John Walker Jackson of Harrisburg to conduct the religious exercises; Rev. Stephen Smith, of Philadelphia, to officiate as President of the day; Gov. A. G. Curtin will review the troops.]
people: President of the day (Rev.), of Philadelphia

articles.headline: Colored Soldiers' and Seamen's U. S. Government Claim Office (John J. Keefe, Jr.)
articles.summary: Colored Soldiers' and Seamen's U. S. Government Claim Office. John J. Keefe, Jr., Attorney, No. 511 S. Sixth St., (below Lombard,) Philadelphia. Soldiers' and Seamen's Claims for U. S. Bounty, State and City Bounty, Pensions, Back Pay, Prize Money, and all other just claims against the United States promptly recovered. Especial attention given to the Claims of Widows and Heirs of Deceased Soldiers and Sailors. ... Patronize your own office, if you want justice, quick returns, and satisfaction. Oct. 28, 3mos.
people: attorney, claim office, No. 511 S. Sixth St. below Lombard

events.name: Zion A. M. E. Mission Church: grand presentation
events.location: Zion A. M. E. Mission Church, 7th street between Dickerson and Fo[?]ter streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice of a grand presentation on October 15th, 1865, at 4 o'clock P. M.: a family Bible, an A. M. E. hymn book, a picture of the reading of President Lincoln's Proclamation, an Evening Scene and a gold pen to be given to the persons who collected the most money toward liquidating the church debt; a collection afterwards for the church; the presentation speech 'by an able speaker' (not named). Bishop Wayman was appointed to preach at Zion Mission the same night.

events.name: Bishop Wayman in Philadelphia: Bethel, Union and Wesley
events.location: Bethel Church (morning), Union Church (afternoon), Wesley Church (night), Philadelphia
events.description: Bishop Wayman's published appointments: Sunday Oct. 8 at Bethel, Union and Wesley; at home Oct. 9 to 13; Oct. 13 Horntown; Sunday Oct. 15 Norristown (morning), Germantown (afternoon), Zion Mission Church, Philadelphia (night); Oct. 16 Lower Valley; Oct. 17 West Chester; then Downingtown, Phoenixville, Lancaster, Marietta, Columbia, and Wrightsville on Oct. 23. The same Sunday the Hurst St. A. M. E. church (J. Mitchel, pastor) held its second quarterly meeting and the First Colored Wesley church on Lombard St. its quarterly meeting with a camp protracted meeting.

events.name: Odd Fellows' celebration and procession at Baltimore (seventh anniversary of the Order), with the Philadelphia lodges
events.location: Baltimore: Mount Vernon Square, Charles, Madison and Calvert streets; Douglass Hall, Lexington St.
events.description: The editor (E. Weaver) went down on the night line of Oct. 5 with over two hundred colored ladies and gentlemen and over two hundred Odd Fellows from Philadelphia. The Order formed in rank at the depot and marched to Douglass Hall, Lexington street. At 10 A. M. on Oct. 6 the procession formed at Mount Vernon Square, right wing on Madison street, and marched along Charles to Madison street headed by a platoon of the city policemen; 'without the slightest molestation from any quarter'. Chief Marshal of the Day, P. N. F. Greenbury D. Martin; aids P. G. M. C. L. J. Lee and J. Scott; Boyer's celebrated band of some twenty performers; Saml. W. Chase Jr., marshal, aids John H. Griffin and James H. Jordan. Order of the lodges: Nehemiah Lodge No. 1210 (36, marshal James Jackson); Second Manasseh Lodge No. 1214 (35, marshal Isadore Oliver); King David Lodge (23, marshal C. Dutton); Mount Lebanon Lodge (47, marshal Alexander W. Cottman); Zerubbabel Lodge No. 1187 (38, marshal J. C. Hamer); Crystal Fount Lodge No. 100 (48, marshal Elwood Fosgood [?]); Olive Lodge No. 987 (40, marshal Joseph S. Chase); Eden Lodge No. 902 (20, marshal W. H. Brown); a car drawn by eight horses carrying seventeen orphan children under the care of the Grand Lodge; George A. Hackett, marshal and guide; the Mozart Brass Band of Washington (Joseph Anbrush [?], leader; Prof. A. T. Lillie instructor); John F. Cook Lodge of Washington (18); Eastern Star and Potomac Lodge No. 1023 of Alexandria (23); Union Friendship Lodge No. 891 of Washington (25); the Delmonico Band of Philadelphia, Jacob Boyer [?] leader; Wm. Gibson, marshal, with aids J. D. Kelly and James W. Brown; Star of Bethlehem Lodge No. 897 of Wilmington, Del. (27); CARTHAGINIAN LODGE No. 1060 OF PHILADELPHIA (21 members); UNITY LODGE No. 711 OF PHILADELPHIA (26 members). Delegations also from the Good Samaritan, Phoenix, Covenant, Friendship, Mount Olive, Mount Lebanon, Fraternal and Good Hope [lodges] of West Philadelphia [the printed list does not make clear which are of Philadelphia], Good Will of Norristown, United Brethren of Wilmington; the Past Noble Fathers (65) and Council No. 5 of Wilmington (55); then the Grand Lodge of the G. U. O. of O. F. with the Ark and emblems; Grand Master James McC. Crummel of Philadelphia with the Deputy Grand Master, Grand Treasurer and Grand Secretary in three barouches. At Mount Vernon Square, before the court house, exercises opened by Rev. William H. Brown, member of the Order and Past Grand Master, with Grand Master J. McC. Crummel presiding; addresses by Rev. Samuel Chase, Patrick H. Reason of New York (brother of Prof. Reason of the High School) and N. F. James H. Jordan of Baltimore; about nineteen hundred present; procession re-formed at 3 P. M. and returned to Douglass Hall; grand supper at night. The editor also met Bishop Daniel A. Payne at Rev. S. L. Hammond's, with Revs. D. Moore, Hebbard [?], Chaplains Turner and Hall [?] and J. M. Brown; visited the True Communicator (Cooke and Williams, editors) and Rev. W. D. W. Schureman's new Gothic church (40 by ? feet) and parsonage; on Sunday Oct. 8 heard Rev. Mr. Mars at Sharp St. (M. E.) and preached at Bethel, Baltimore; Payne preached at Bethel in the morning and John M. Brown at night. Weaver and Payne returned on Monday Oct. 9.
attendees: Grand Master, G. U. O. of O. F., of Philadelphia

events.name: Union A. M. E. Church, Coates St.: all-day special sermons and collection
events.location: Union A. M. E. Church, Coates St., Philadelphia
events.description: General invitation to special sermons throughout the day, Sabbath Oct. 29; speakers engaged: Bishop Wayman (printed 'Weymen'), Revs. W. Moore, W. D. W. Schureman, N. H. Turpin, D. P. Seaton, J. Hamilton and others; a large collection hoped for. Signed by the Elder, Richard P. G[?] (surname uncertain). Bishop Wayman's own appointment list (Oct 21) placed him at Union Church that afternoon after a dedication at Deep Cut, Camden.

notes: CR_1865-10-07: p1 is poetry, H. R. Revels's letter from Vicksburg (Sept 12), a letter from Hannibal Mo. (signed 'Hannibal'; Rev. J. H. Turpin), Annie M. Smith of Xenia on charity, John Jones of Chicago on colored Masons (Prince Hall history), 'The Mother's Prayer' (J. M. Neilan), the Wilberforce subscription lists of the Ohio and Indiana Conferences (J. A. Shorter), W. H. Waters from Hagerstown: all non-Philadelphia, not entered.

CR_1865-10-07 p2: two letters from Harrisburg (the pastor on his quarterly meeting and the State Equal Rights League and Home Protection League assembled there, dated Oct. 3; and 'Equal Rights' on the Garnett Equal Rights League No. 1 of Harrisburg: Rev. John E. Price president, vice presidents Martin Perry, Jos. B. Popel, Mrs. Annie E. Amos, Miss L. C. Williams, treasurer Miss Mary Williams, secretary Alexander T. Harris, T. Morris Chester honorary member; Prof. Wm. Howard Day to lecture Friday the 13th; a second 'John Brown League' in the western part of the city). Non-Philadelphia: text only.

CR_1865-10-07 p2: editorial puff for E. Matlack & Son's clothing store (904 Market St.; white firm, new ad dated Oct. 7 on p3) not entered. 'Notice to Our Readers': the editor thinks of converting the fourth page to political discussion of the rights of our people.

CR_1865-10-07 repeats not re-entered (p3 and p4): Mrs. Amelia W. Adams's select school (Juniper St.); Abraham Fields's New Grocery and Provision Store (now read as No. 424 South Seventh St., third door above the corner of Lombard); Lincoln Monument; Georgina Gleaves; Mrs. H. T. O'Donnell; S. Shorter Hawkins (615 Lombard); T. J. Bowers's small ad; R. H. Gleaves; Maria Highgates; William Still's stove store; Olive Branch; Mrs. M. Bennett; Bustill wig makers; N. L. Durham; James C. Clark M.D.; Mrs. Ann E. Foster; Book Depository; Longfellow; Jane Johnson and Ann Wear, shrouding (618 South Eighth); Duterte; Charnock; Mrs. C. E. Harding; James W. Brown, steam dyeing; Charles W. Brister; Mrs. M. C. Gibbons's intelligence office. Out of town or white: Globe Hotel and William P. Powell (New York), Henderson's clothing, Magarge paper, Matlack, Jones' One Price Clothing, Reimer, Costar, Mason & Hamlin, Penna. Central R. R., Washington Hotel (Georgetown), Hudson's City Hotel and Dr. J. W. Creek (Baltimore), Avery College, Jane Jobs (Fairhaven N. J.), Jas. B. Rodgers printer.
CR_1865-10-07: 'J. Mitchel' / 'J. Mitchell' of the Hurst St. (Wesley) A. M. E. church is the same pastor in the notice and the marriage; recorded as printed in each.

CR_1865-10-14 p1: Wm. B. Young's verse; Rev. J. M. Brown(?) on missions; letter from Louisville; letter from Washington; 'Notes by the Way'; Charleston correspondence; a reported sermon 'Victory and Eternity'; 'A Resolution' of the American Baptist Missionary Convention (moved by Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller) thanking the Anglo-African and the Christian Recorder. All non-Philadelphia or devotional: not entered.

CR_1865-10-14 p2: Annie M. Smith's Xenia, Ohio letter (Emancipation celebration, Sept 22; Chaplain E. D. Davis, J. R. Blackburn, Elder P. Lowery of Tennessee, Langston): text only. 'Glorious News from Wilmington' (Del.), 'Letter from H. J. Young', 'Why Copperheads Oppose Negro Suffrage', 'Contribution to the Album of Love' and the American Christian Commission item: not entered.

CR_1865-10-14: the Baltimore Odd Fellows celebration was announced in Run #93; this is the REPORT (new). The marshal printed 'Wm. Gibson' and aid 'James W. Brown' are given only as the Philadelphia band/division marshals; 'James W. Brown' could be the steam dyer of that name but nothing in the item says so.

CR_1865-10-14 repeats not re-entered: page 4 entirely as Oct. 7 (Globe Hotel and W. P. Powell, Henderson, Magarge, African Civilization Society, Wolcott, St. Charles Hotel, Wilson's map-mounting, Dandridge Kelly, Book Store catalogue, Mrs. M. C. Gibbons's Intelligence Office now read as No. 1113 Pine, Book Depository, Longfellow 1126 Rodman, Jane Johnson and Ann Wear 618 S. Eighth, Duterte 634 Lombard, Champion, Charnock 427 S. 6th, Mrs. C. E. Harding 713 Lombard, Avery College, James W. Brown's steam-dyeing (No. 129 [?] S. Fifth above Walnut and 1003 Shippen), Brister 717 Lombard, Jane Jobs, Rodgers). Page 3: Richard Parker's information wanted (entered Oct 7), Brainerd, Adams school, Matlack, Bowers, Fields, Lincoln Monument, Gleaves, O'Donnell (now 913 [?] Lombard, formerly 740 South), Creek, R. H. Gleaves, Highgates (1026 Barley), Still's stove store (Oct 1 date), Olive Branch (Mrs. H. M. Cropper, 814 Lombard), Bennett, Bustill, Durham, Clark, Foster, Hudson's City Hotel.

CR_1865-10-14 p3: Rev. A. Till's wedding: 'Rev. W. Moore' officiated; the obituary's 'William Moore, the son of Chas. and Emily B?ed' is a different person (18 years old). 'Olive Cemetery' as printed.
CR_1865-10-14: the aid 'J. D. Kelly' (Philadelphia division, Baltimore parade) may be the 'Joshua D. Kelly [?]' of the Oct 28 Harrisburg committee; not merged.

CR_1865-10-21 p1: 'Teach Me to Watch and Pray' (verse); an interesting letter from (Ohio?); Albany correspondence signed Wm. W. Grimes (Rhode Island school law; Mr. Downing, F. T. Waugh, Rev. Parker); 'Letter from the Queen City' (Cincinnati, Oct. 11; Bro. Shorter at Allen Chapel, Bro. Shelton at Zion, Bro. Newman of Mound St.), with an account of a 'tin wedding' of Mr. and Mrs. Alexandria Thomas on Longworth Street, Cincinnati, signed F. O. B.; Detroit correspondence (lecture of Rev. H. H. Garnet; J. D. Richards, chair; signed M.); letter from Gainesville, Fla. (H. S. Harmon, Co. B, 3d U.S.C.T.); New London, Ind. correspondence (W. J. Davis); 'The Evening Walk' (Annie M. Smith, Xenia); 'The Newly Organized Churches of the South' (Rev. James Lynch); 'The Freedmen's Conference in Philadelphia' (reprinted from The Methodist: on the Delaware colored conference of the M. E. Church, severed from the Philadelphia Annual Conference); 'How It Was Done'. No Philadelphia names: not entered.

CR_1865-10-21 p2: 'The Parade of Monday' is the grand parade of the FIREMEN of Philadelphia and other cities (Monday Oct. 16), column eight miles long; no Black participation mentioned; not entered as a procession of the community. 'The 14th U.S. Colored Heavy Artillery' (arrival in New York, to be disbanded): no names. Other p2 items (Negro suffrage in Connecticut, Convention of colored men in Virginia, Zabadiah Smith, St. Louis meeting, Douglass Institute of Baltimore, Sumner's letter on the amendment, Charleston correspondence, letter from Hannibal, reception of the 5th Ohio regiment, Harrisburg letter, Wilmington letter) are non-Philadelphia.

CR_1865-10-21 p3 c1: 'The Society of Inquiry on Missions' (Wilberforce): D. A. Payne re-elected president, J. P. Shorter 1st vice president, Miss M. E. Ashe [?] 2d vice president, Miss ? Brown [?] recording secretary, James E. Porter corresponding secretary; signed T. H. Jackson, Cor. Sec'y S. I. M. Ohio: text only.

CR_1865-10-21: 'Nath. L. Durham' (Prudence Lodge committee) is very probably the N. L. Durham, cupping and leeching, 911 1/2 Christian St., whose ad runs on the same page (printed there 'Nathaniel L. Durham'); identification for the owner, not merged.

CR_1865-10-21: Richard Parker's 'Information Wanted' and the New York District preachers' notice repeat (entered Oct 7 and Oct 14). Page 4 entirely repeats (see Oct 14 note; Gibbons's office printed '1113 Pine' again, Harding's 'Philadelphia, Oct., 1864'). Page 3 ad columns 4-7 repeat Oct 7 and Oct 14 (Fields, Lincoln Monument, Gleaves, O'Donnell, Bowers, Highgates, Still, Hawkins's fall goods, Olive Branch, Bennett, Bustill, Durham, Clark, Foster).

CR_1865-10-28 p1: 'Where Would You Have Him?' (verse); Leavenworth correspondence; letter from Port Deposit, Md.; mass meeting in Edgecombe Co., N. C.; letter from Richmond; the colored convention in North Carolina and its address to the Constitutional Convention (J. H. Harris, chairman; John R. Good, George A. Rue, Isham Swett, J. Randolph Jr., committee); 'A Voice from Michigan' (Wm. J. Anderson, Niles); semi-annual report of the Genesee A. M. E. Zion Conference Missionary Society (Rev. J. W. Loguen, agent). All non-Philadelphia: not entered.

CR_1865-10-28 p2: editorial correspondence 'Notes by the Way' (Weaver's trip to Cincinnati and St. Louis with Rev. John M. Brown; refused proper dinner at Seymour, Ind.); Detroit correspondence; 'Young Men, Arouse!'; the hanging of Magruder at Louisville; the Episcopal consultation; John M. Brown from Norfolk (Sept 26); 'Letter from Camden' on the elective franchise signed only 'A. B.' (Camden, N. J., Oct. 25 [?], 1865); 'Going South' (D. Cooper, Greenfield, Ohio); the Aberdeen Freedmen's Aid Society meeting (Scotland). Not entered.

CR_1865-10-28: Sarah M. Douglass (661 N. 13th St.) is very probably the teacher Sarah Mapps Douglass; identification for the owner only, recorded as printed and not linked pending the address check (see flags).

CR_1865-10-28: the Harrisburg reception committee lists 'Jacob C. White, Jr.' plainly (cf. the 'Jacob O. White' misprint of Oct 21). 'Thos. J. Bowers' on the committee = the coal dealer of 634 Lombard (same printed name as his ad); 'Jos. C. Bustill' per owner's merge = Joseph Cassey Bustill. Identifications in notes only.

CR_1865-10-28 repeats not re-entered: page 4 entirely (Mrs. C. E. Harding's dry goods ad now reads '712 Lombard Street' in both places on this printing, versus 713 in the brief's list: an address change or a misprint for the owner to check); Hamilton E. Waters's notice (now adds Rinaldo Turner, Sandy Anderson and Wm. Heady); Adams's school (now '609 [?] Juniper St., between Spruce and Pine'), Matlack, Fields, Lincoln Monument and the other page 3 standing ads. The Lincoln Monument ad now lists Rev. [J.?] B.
